title: Relative smooth strict normal crossings pairs under arbitrary field extension
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $L/F$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $X$ be a smooth finite-type $F$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $D\subseteq X$ be a relative smooth strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor], with distinct integral components $(D_a)_{a\in A}$ for a finite set $A$. Put $X_L=X\times_F L$ and $D_L=D\times_F L$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $X_L$ is smooth over $L$, and $D_L$ is reduced effective Cartier [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal, def-pc-reduced-scheme] and is a relative smooth strict normal crossings divisor over $L$. More precisely, each $(D_a)_L$ is smooth and is a finite disjoint union of integral open and closed components; these, as $a$ varies, are exactly the distinct integral components of $D_L$. For any $r$ distinct such components, their scheme-theoretic intersection is empty or smooth over $L$ of pure codimension $r$ in $X_L$. If two chosen components come from the same $D_a$, the intersection is empty. For components indexed by distinct $a\in J\subseteq A$, the intersection is an open and closed subscheme of $(\bigcap_{a\in J}D_a)_L$. The empty intersection is $X_L$, of pure codimension zero in itself. The assertions include $D=\varnothing$ and $X=\varnothing$. No separability assumption is imposed on $L/F$.

proof.text: For $J\subseteq A$ put $Y_J=\bigcap_{a\in J}D_a$, with $Y_\varnothing=X$. The SNC definition makes every $Y_J/F$ smooth. Each $Y_J$ is a closed subscheme of the finite-type scheme $X$: on a finite affine cover its coordinate ring is a quotient of a finitely generated $F$-algebra, generated by the images of the same generators. Thus every $Y_J/F$ is of finite type. Finite-type base change gives finite type over $L$ for $X_L$ and $(Y_J)_L$, and smooth base change gives smoothness. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma makes all these schemes Noetherian. Smooth geometric normality, applied also to the trivial extension $F/F$, makes $X,Y_J,X_L,(Y_J)_L$ normal and reduced. Clause (2) of the normal-component lemma therefore decomposes each into finitely many disjoint integral open and closed components. In particular each $(D_a)_L$ has precisely the asserted finite decomposition.

Write $p:X_L\to X$. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}R_L$, where $R_L=R\otimes_F L$, by the affine fibre-product theorem. The map $R\to R_L$ is faithfully flat by the field-extension base-change lemma. Consequently $p$ is flat, and flat pullback of an effective Cartier ideal applied to $D$ gives that $D_L$ is effective Cartier. Explicitly a local equation $t$ for $D$ remains a nonzerodivisor in $R_L$. No separability or algebraicity of $L/F$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 02OO (lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined), case (6); schemes.tex Tags 01I4 and 01JQ for the affine fibre product.

proof.text: On the preceding affine chart let $I_a\subseteq R$ define $D_a$, so $D$ is defined by $I=\bigcap_a I_a$. The kernel of the diagonal map $R\to\bigoplus_a R/I_a$ is $I$. Tensor this exact sequence over $F$ with $L$: a field module is flat, and the flat-tensor-exact lemma preserves the kernel. Hence the kernel of $R_L\to\bigoplus_a(R/I_a)\otimes_F L$ is $IR_L$, equivalently $IR_L=\bigcap_a I_aR_L$. (Tensor distributes over this finite sum by its defining bilinear universal property.) This proves that $D_L$ is the scheme-theoretic union of the $(D_a)_L$. Each factor $(R/I_a)\otimes_F L$ is reduced by Step 1; the induced injection $R_L/IR_L\hookrightarrow\bigoplus_a(R/I_a)\otimes_F L$ shows that $R_L/IR_L$ has no nonzero nilpotents. Thus $D_L$ is reduced. For an empty family $I=R$ and the quotient is the zero ring, giving the empty divisor.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), with Tag 00HB (definition-flat); affine kernel calculation and the SNC scheme-theoretic-union definition.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty component $V$ of some nonempty $Y_J$, and let $\eta$ be its generic point. The finite clopen decomposition in Step 1 places $V$ inside a unique integral clopen component $U$ of $X$. Indeed its intersections with the finitely many such components are a disjoint clopen cover of the irreducible space $V$. These components are of finite type, being closed subschemes of finite-type schemes as in Step 1. Set $n=\dim U$ and $m=\dim V$; both are finite by dimension finiteness. Dimension constancy on irreducible locally algebraic schemes gives $\dim_x X=n$ and $\dim_xY_J=m$ for every $x\in V$. At $\eta$ the local ring of $Y_J$ is the fraction field of the integral component $V$, so it has dimension zero. On any affine neighbourhood in $X$, $\eta$ corresponds to a minimal prime over the defining ideal of $Y_J$. Its height is $|J|$ by the SNC hypothesis. This equals $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$: chains of primes in the localization at this prime are exactly the chains of primes contained in it. Applying the dimension-at-a-point formula to $X$ and $Y_J$ at $\eta$, whose residue fields are identical for a closed immersion, gives $n=|J|+\operatorname{trdeg}_F\kappa(\eta)$ and $m=\operatorname{trdeg}_F\kappa(\eta)$. Thus $\dim_x X=\dim_xY_J+|J|$ for every $x\in Y_J$. This argument is componentwise and makes no equidimensionality assumption on $X$.

source.place: Tag 02FX (lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point); varieties.tex Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), part (3); the SNC minimal-prime height hypothesis.

proof.text:
For $y\in (Y_J)_L$ with image $x\in Y_J$, apply fibre-dimension invariance twice, to $X/F$ and $Y_J/F$. It gives $\dim_y X_L=\dim_xX$ and $\dim_y (Y_J)_L=\dim_xY_J$, hence by Step 4 their difference is $|J|$. Apply the dimension-at-a-point formula over $L$ to these two finite-type schemes at $y$. Their residue fields are the same because the latter is a closed subscheme, so cancellation gives
$$\dim\mathcal O_{X_L,y}=\dim\mathcal O_{(Y_J)_L,y}+|J|.$$
At a generic point $z$ of any component of $(Y_J)_L$, its local ring is a field by the integral clopen decomposition of Step 1. Therefore $\dim\mathcal O_{X_L,z}=|J|$. Equivalently every minimal prime over the defining ideal of $(Y_J)_L$ in every ambient affine chart has height $|J|$, by the same localization-of-prime-chains argument as in Step 4. This proves the required pure codimension for the whole pulled-back intersection, and the displayed equality also holds at every point of it.

Choose $r$ members $C_1,\ldots,C_r$ of the clopen integral decompositions of the $(D_a)_L$. If two distinct chosen members lie in the same $(D_a)_L$, they are disjoint even as subschemes (their fibre product is the empty open intersection), so the full intersection is empty. Otherwise their original indices form $J\subseteq A$ with $|J|=r$. The universal property of fibre products identifies $\bigcap_{a\in J}(D_a)_L$ with $(Y_J)_L$: both classify maps to $X_L$ factoring through all these closed subschemes. Its projection to each $(D_a)_L$ pulls the chosen clopen component back to a clopen subscheme. Intersecting these finitely many clopen subschemes gives exactly $Z=\bigcap_i C_i$. Thus $Z$ is an open and closed subscheme of $(Y_J)_L$. Its local rings at its points are those of $(Y_J)_L$, so it is smooth over $L$ by the affine-local characterization of smoothness in the cited definition: an affine chart of this open subscheme is an affine open of the smooth source, with the same structure map. The height calculation of Step 5 at its component generic points gives pure codimension $r$ in $X_L$.

source.place: Tag 01JP (definition-fibre-product), associativity by its universal property; smoothness on open restrictions follows directly from the affine-local characterization (Tag 01V5) in def-sbc-smooth-morphisms.

proof.text: The integral pieces from different original indices are also pairwise noncontained. Otherwise let $C\subseteq (D_a)_L$ have its support contained in that of a piece $C'\subseteq (D_b)_L$, $a\ne b$, and let $\xi$ be the generic point of $C$. The intersection $Z=C\cap C'$ is a closed subscheme of $C$. Its local ring at $\xi$ is a nonzero quotient of the field $\mathcal O_{C,\xi}$, hence that field. Step 6 makes $Z$ clopen in $(Y_{\{a,b\}})_L$, so the formula of Step 5 gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X_L,\xi}=2$. But $C$ is clopen in $(D_a)_L$, whose local ring at $\xi$ is the same field, and the formula for $J=\{a\}$ gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X_L,\xi}=1$, a contradiction. Pieces from the same index are already disjoint. Consequently the entire finite family consists of pairwise noncontained integral closed subschemes. By Step 3 it has scheme-theoretic union $D_L$: splitting a scheme into clopen components does not change its union. An irreducible subset of a finite union of closed sets lies in one of them (induct on the finite family in the definition of irreducibility); noncontainment then shows these pieces are exactly the distinct irreducible components of $D_L$.

source.place: Tag 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian), combined with the preceding pointwise dimension formula; identification of components uses the finite-union definition of irreducibility.

proof.text: Steps 1--3 give smoothness of $X_L$ and the reduced effective Cartier divisor $D_L$. Steps 6--7 give its finite integral-component presentation with pairwise noncontained supports and all nonempty intersections smooth of the stated pure codimension. These are precisely the clauses of the smooth strict normal crossings definition. When $r=0$, the defining fibre product has no conditions, so its intersection is $X_L$, smooth of codimension zero in itself (its minimal primes have height zero). If $D=\varnothing$, its ideal is the unit ideal and stays so after tensoring; the component family is empty. If $X=\varnothing$ all these assertions are vacuous and the empty intersection is again $X_L=\varnothing$. Every step used an arbitrary field extension; no separability hypothesis has entered.
